sum: Combinations of millet extract, L-cystine, keratin and B vitamins, sold for hair loss.
b: Telogen hair shedding (after stress, illness or childbirth)
w: Hair loss is often caused by iron deficiency, thyroid problems or hormones: check these first. If it contains biotin, it distorts thyroid and troponin tests.

sum: A red, tart tea made from the calyces of the hibiscus flower.
w: May lower blood pressure too much together with blood pressure medicines. Interacts with hydrochlorothiazide and paracetamol. Avoid in pregnancy.

sum: A polyphenol from olive oil and olives, with an approved EU health claim.
b: Approved EFSA claim at 5 mg/day from olive oil
w: Generally safe. Prefer olive oil as food.

sum: A resin from the mastic tree of Chios. The European Medicines Agency recognises it as a traditional herbal medicine for mild indigestion.
b: One small Greek study and traditional use
Low eradication in small studies, does not replace antibiotics
fd: Mastic as a spice in sweets and bread
w: Generally safe. Possible allergy in people allergic to pistachios (same plant family). Persistent heartburn needs a doctor.

n: Magnesium on the skin (spray, oil, Epsom salts)
sum: Magnesium chloride or sulphate applied to the skin or added to a bath.
b: Meaningful absorption through the skin has not been shown
Small studies, massage may be what helps
fd: Leafy greens, nuts, legumes, whole grains
w: May sting or irritate the skin. For a deficiency, magnesium by mouth is the evidence-based choice.

sum: The fruit of the wild rose, with vitamin C and galactolipids.
w: Generally safe. Caution with kidney stones and anticoagulants.
May bind medicines and nutrients: keep at least 2 hours apart from medicines. Some products contain lead or aluminium. Constipation.
